passage:
Archaeologists found writing scratched onto a wall in an old building. It was not official writing. It was more like a personal message.
Students laughed because people long ago had also written on walls. The teacher used the moment to discuss what counts as historical evidence.
Official records show what leaders wanted remembered. Informal writing shows ordinary voices, jokes, complaints, and names.
The wall writing was not polite, but it was valuable.
History is richer when it includes imperfect human marks. A scratched sentence can prove that someone stood there, felt something, and wanted to leave a trace.
